hypothesis: Separating the existing SPCX Swing/HA entry rows by long and short direction or shifting their causal entry clock may produce a repeatable after-cost mechanism across development and validation without dependence on one winner.
decision: Reject the tested static side and entry-timing set. Provider-exact, alignment-onset, next-bar-confirmation, and first-fast-EMA-pullback arms produced no timing/side combination that remained nonempty, net-positive, above PF 1, and positive after removing its largest winner in both development and validation under nominal and stress friction. Do not queue another generic long/short split of this route. Any further SPCX Swing challenger must declare a new causal mechanism identity and use a preregistered test; this revision does not alter the current v25 runtime.
falsifier: This decision is invalidated by source-hash mismatch, altered trade rows, leakage from the sealed holdout, a changed fill clock or friction contract, or failure to reproduce all 32 timing-side-partition-friction cells. A new causal SPCX mechanism may update the conclusion only if it is specified before evaluation and survives after costs, chronological partitions, and largest-winner removal; the result does not establish that no SPCX strategy can work.
limitations: Development and validation were already opened and cannot serve as a sealed promotion test.
The sealed holdout remains unread; no holdout metric was used.
The results are independent-asset 15-minute approximations rather than a shared-router replay.
Visible-book and latency friction are modeled rather than realized venue fills.
The test exhausts four existing entry clocks and two sides, not the space of all possible SPCX mechanisms.
This revision is report-only and cannot route, size, enter, close, restart, pause, or promote a strategy.
